subject: Token delivery commitments for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints
messages:
From: Lisa Huang <lisa@acme-platform.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Platform Engineering <infra@acme-platform.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify token delivery expectations for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints

Jonas — thanks for the demo today. A couple of follow-ups from the engineering and procurement teams as we scope the pilot:

1) We need clear commitments on time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming endpoints vs latency expectations for non-streaming generation. We observed variability in the trial where TTFT ranged from ~120ms to >450ms depending on model variant and prompt length.

2) For streaming: we care about (a) initial TTFT for the first token, and (b) sustained token delivery rate (tokens/sec) once the stream is alive. For our conversational use case we’d like to target ~200ms TTFT and ~1,200–1,500 tokens/sec sustained for the most common paths. Can Redwood commit to those numbers, or provide an exception process if certain models or quantized builds cannot meet them?

3) For non-streaming batch runs (large offline generations) we expect higher TTFT but are focused on aggregate throughput and P95 completion times. We want to understand your P95 targets and any credits or remediation if SLAs aren’t met.

Attached are a few example logs and sample prompts (latency-samples-acme-20260517.log). Procurement: please let us know if we should loop legal before we discuss formal wording.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Huang
Director, Product infra — ACME Platform

Attachments: latency-samples-acme-20260517.log (stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Huang <lisa@acme-platform.com>
Cc: ACME Platform Engineering <infra@acme-platform.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify token delivery expectations for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints

Hi Lisa — great questions and thanks for the logs. I ran these by infra and our runtime team; below is a concise, pragmatic proposal that balances what we can guarantee today and how we handle exceptions.

Proposal (streaming endpoints):
- Commitment: P95 TTFT <= 300ms for interactive prompts (prompt length <= 128 tokens) under agreed concurrency and model selection.
- Sustained delivery: median tokens/sec >= 1,200 for the stream once first token delivered, tested on our streaming-optimized model variants.
- Exception case: some quantized model variants and very long prompt+context windows can bump TTFT or reduce token/sec. For those specific model builds we propose a documented exception process (see below).

Proposal (non-streaming / batch endpoints):
- Commitment: P95 completion latency targets will be scoped by model family and prompt length; e.g., medium-size generations (~512 tokens) P95 <= 1.2s per 100 tokens under reserved capacity.
- Throughput: when using Dedicated capacity, throughput guarantees are a function of reserved GPU pools and concurrency limits; we’ll include concrete numbers in the performance addendum.

Exception & remediation process (summary):
- Pilot exception: we can offer a 90-day streaming-exception window for ACME to validate the streaming-optimized variants at scale. During this window we will:
  * Run a controlled canary against a subset of production traffic (details below).
  * Provide dashboard access to token-level traces and a daily SLA report.
  * Commit to a remediation plan if P95 TTFT > 350ms for more than 5% of requests across the monitoring window.
- Credits: if the remediation criteria are met without sufficient mitigation within the agreed window, we propose a service credit equal to 25% of monthly usage for the affected endpoints for that billing month (subject to legal review).

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm whether ACME wants a hard P95 300ms or is comfortable with the pilot-style 300->350ms guardrails, 2) sign a short performance addendum (I’ll attach a draft), 3) schedule a 60-minute runbook/canary planning call with infra and our runtime leads.

I’ve attached a draft performance addendum and a short benchmark summary. Happy to walk through specifics on the call.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-performance-addendum-draft.pdf (stub), benchmark-summary-2026-05.png (stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarify token delivery expectations for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints

Jonas / Marissa — forwarding ACME’s ask and Jonas’s proposal. Quick internal decision: we can greenlight a limited pilot exception but with firm guardrails.

Please note the approvals/conditions we require before committing publicly to SLAs:
- Approval window: 90-day pilot exception from go-live with telemetry turned on and daily SLA reports shared with ACME.
- Concurrency cap: pilot limited to 50 concurrent streaming sessions per region. If ACME needs higher concurrency we’ll re-evaluate after benchmark results.
- SLO deviation & credits: if P95 TTFT > 350ms for >5% of requests in any 24h reporting window we will trigger remediation. If remediation fails within 7 business days, credit = 25% of affected endpoint monthly usage (subject to MSA amendment).
- Model constraints: exception applies only to specified streaming-optimized model variants; other models remain governed by standard performance profiles.
- Legal/Procurement: require a short performance addendum and authorizing signature from ACME procurement. Marissa — please prepare the addendum with the credit language and telemetry requirements.

Jonas — coordinate the canary plan with infra and include the verification scripts (we’ll need reproducible test harness and the Drive link with test prompts).

Hannah
VP, Sales Operations (interim)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Token delivery commitments for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints — pilot terms and next steps

Lisa — thanks, and appreciate the quick reviews from your side. Per our internal approvals, here’s the finalized pilot agreement in plain language and next steps: 

Summary of commitments (pilot):
- Streaming endpoints: target P95 TTFT <= 300ms for interactive prompts (<=128 tokens). Pilot guardrail allows P95 up to 350ms as an exception; if >5% of requests breach 350ms in a 24h window we trigger remediation steps.
- Tokens/sec: median sustained delivery >=1,200 tokens/sec for the stream on the agreed model variants; we'll publish daily tokens/sec histograms during the pilot.
- Non-streaming endpoints: P95 completion targets scoped per model family; we’ll include exact numbers in the addendum.
- Credits & remediation: 25% credit on affected endpoint usage if remediation is not completed within 7 business days after an SLA breach trigger (MSA amendment required).
- Telemetry: Redwood will give ACME read access to a dashboard with token-level traces and daily report exports.
- Duration & concurrency: 90-day pilot starting on the agreed go-live date, concurrency limited to 50 streaming sessions per region during pilot.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to share the performance addendum draft and MSA amendment (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-minute canary planning call this week — proposed slots: Thu 05/21 10:00am PT or Fri 05/22 9:00am PT.
3) ACME to confirm whether the pilot concurrency cap fits their initial traffic pattern; if not, tell us the expected peak and we’ll re-scope.

I’ve attached the performance addendum and a sample benchmark report for the variants we plan to run in the canary. Please review and let me know which call slot works. Once ACME signs the addendum we’ll provision telemetry and start the canary.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
